author: Terrell Boettcher
title: School board hires Matt Albrecht as boys basketball coach - NewsBreak
text:
By Terrell Boettcher ,
22 hours ago The Hayward School Board voted Monday June 1 to hire Matt Albrecht as Hurricane boys basketball head coach, replacing Curtis DeCora.
Albrecht, a former Hayward player and graduate, has 16 years of experience coaching basketball in Hayward.
According to the board agenda, there were three applicants for the head coach position.
In other actions Monday, the board:
—Approved a March 3-8, 2027 trip to Nashville for the Hayward High School Choir. Director Ben DiSera said the choir will perform four times during their trip and will visit a Grand Ol’ Opry show, Andrew Jackson’s home, Country Music Hall of Fame, Johnny Cash museum and Studio B recording studio. The trip is organized by Performance Tours.
The choir will be part of a master class at Vanderbilt University.
—Thanked Kelly Ryder for her nine years of service as district curriculum and programs director.
—Approved a bid of $29,189 from Luedtke Landscaping and Tree Service for renovating the varsity softball field, starting after July 1. Half of the cost will come from a donation from the American Birkebeiner Ski Foundation (ABSF).
—Approved letters of resignation from Shawn Martinson, JV boys basketball coach; Ken Vessel, eighth grade girls basketball coach, Zach Noreen, eighth grade boys basketball coach; Orrin Botten as high school boys golf coach (12 years of service); and Stephanie Poplin as photography advisor.
—Approved the transfer of Lauren Prince from part-time to full-time high school administrative assistant; Trista Wiley from special education aide to intervention aide; and Nicole Schlapper from first grade teacher to fourth grade teacher.
—Voted to hire Gene Richardson as high school custodian.
—The board’s policy committee approved the first reading of Policy 5136 for student use of personal communication devices (cell phones) to meet new state requirements. According to state law, the policy must be in place by July 1.
The policy states that “Students may use PCDs before and after school, during their lunch break, in between classes as long as they do not create a distraction, disruption or otherwise interfere with the educational environment, during after-school activities (e.g., extra‑curricular activities), or at school-related functions.
“Use of PCDs, except those approved by a teacher or administrator, at any other time is prohibited and they must be powered completely off (i.e., not just placed into vibrate or silent mode) and stored out of sight.
“Students may not use PCDs on school property or at a school-sponsored activity to access and/or view Internet websites that are otherwise blocked to students at school.”
The facilities committee forwarded to the full board a 3-year bid from Bartingale Mechanical for heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) preventative maintenance and repair.
The board discussed the proposed Veterans Recognition Wall at the high school. Supt. Mark Berquist said the projected cost is just over $5,000.
The board viewed a video of student highlights from the 2025-26 school year, produced by Janell Disher and Mary Hager.
